text:
incident-bot: PAGE: High queue depth observed on runtime-gateway (us-east-1). 95th queue latency >= 3s, inflight nearing capacity. Severity: P1. Grafana: https://grafana.internal/d/rtg/runtime-queues

Alice M.: oncall here, investigating. Pulling up tail and traces.

Ben K.: I'm seeing a big bump in KV cache misses + sustained long tail. Might be partially caused by a recent backend rollout. Suggest temporary runtime mitigations: reduce max_inflight for non-enterprise tenants and enable soft-eviction on low-priority lanes.

Carlos R.: copying. Which tenants to treat as high-priority? I can start customer comms after we decide.

Alice M.: Priority list = tenant-123 (enterprise), tenant-789 (enterprise). All others = soft-shed target. Keep dedicated pools untouched.

Priya S.: ready to flip. Proposed change: 
```
# runtime config change (admin API)
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal/api/v1/runtime/flags" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"max_inflight_default":6, "soft_eviction":true, "low_priority_timeout_s":30}'
```
I'll stage to canary (1 host) then roll.

Ben K.: +1. Also set tenant override for free tier rate limit to 50r/s (was 200r/s) while we stabilize. That will limit pressure from noisy small tenants.

Priya S.: applying canary now -> patch id rtg-4567. Rolling to 10% hosts.

Alice M.: monitoring. Dashboard shows queue depth starting to drop on canary hosts. 95th queue latency on canary down to ~1.1s.

Ben K.: rolling to 100% now. Will watch KV cache warm-up.

Carlos R.: I'm drafting a short note for impacted customers: "We're rate-limiting non-enterprise traffic to reduce latency for SLA customers; we expect normal service within ~15 minutes." Sending to legal for review.

Priya S.: roll complete, change id rtg-4567 -> 100%. Post-change metrics: 95th queue latency global ~1.3s (was 3.2s), inflight headroom recovered. Seeing increase in 429s for experimental/free tenants as expected.

Alice M.: good. For tenants that are seeing 429s we can temporarily apply tenant-specific higher timeout or bump their override if they have active contracts. Priya, can you list top 10 tenants receiving 429s?

Priya S.: top offenders: tenant-exp-42, tenant-free-9, tenant-benchmark-1. I'm applying a conservative timeout bump to tenant-benchmark-1 (45s) because it's a long-polling workload.

Ben K.: note: lowered low_priority_timeout_s from 30 -> 45 for that tenant only. Keep default 30s for others.

Alice M.: status check: any remaining elevated errors?

Priya S.: errors down overall. 429 rate for free tier peaked but trending down. Latency SLOs for enterprise tenants restored.

Carlos R.: I posted the customer note to #customer-watch and sent targeted messages to tenant-123 and tenant-789. They acknowledged.

Alice M.: marking incident mitigated. Will leave this thread open for 1hr to watch for regressions. Postmortem owners: Ben + Priya. Action items: 1) add autoscale policy for runtime queue pressure, 2) build a playbook snippet for tenant overrides, 3) investigate recent backend rollout that correlates with spike.

Priya S.: adding Jira tickets now: RTG-789 (autoscale), RTG-790 (playbook).

Ben K.: I'll pin relevant dashboards and add a test that simulates KV cache warm-up to prevent future sharp tails.

Alice M.: thanks all. :white_check_mark: Closing mitigation phase. We'll follow up in postmortem doc.
